GRANULARITY DIVERGENCE: ZH merged two distinct EN objects into one. e46 = Example 7, polynomials of degree <= n (a function space); e06 = polynomials of degree = n is NOT a linear space (closure fails). z11 states both in a single object (poly<=n function space, plus the degree=n contrast). ZH treated the two polynomial facts as one entry.

GRANULARITY DIVERGENCE: EN merged the first axiom group (Axioms 1 and 2, closure under addition and under scalar multiplication) into one object e55; ZH split it into z22 (Axiom 1, the sum) and z52 (Axiom 2, the product ax) as two separate axiom objects.

GRANULARITY DIVERGENCE: EN e02 is the entire third axiom group (Axioms 7,8,9,10: multiplication by numbers). ZH captured only Axiom 10 (z55, 1x=x); Axioms 7-9 are not present on the ZH side. z55 is a proper subset/special case of e02.

EN-only group object: e11 is the second axiom group (Axioms 3-6: commutativity, associativity, zero, negatives). ZH has no group-summary counterpart. ZH captured only Axiom 5 (z26) and Axiom 6 (z29) individually, which matched EN's own individual axiom objects e12/e48; Axioms 3 and 4 appear on neither side. The 'second group' aggregation is unique to the EN extraction.
EN-only: Example 12, solutions of the homogeneous ODE y''+ay'+by=0 form a function space (nonhomogeneous fails closure). No ZH object covers this differential-equation example.

EN-only: Example 7, the n exponentials e^{a_k x} with distinct a_k are independent (proof by induction). No ZH object covers this.
